Resolve standalone composition errors and clarify definition vs instance aggregation
    fill, including bml:container and bml:with usage.
341.idea: A how-to for fixing composition placement

342.name: FixExpressionErrors
342.documentation:
Procedure when an expression-related BML_EXPR_* (or embed) diagnostic is reported:
1. Confirm host context — member ${ } vs implementation <$ $> (doc:EmbeddedExpressions).
2. Syntax errors — check delimiters, quotes, operators; embeds must not nest <$ $>.
3. Unknown property — verify member exists in scope; StructType fields by name only (not [0]).
4. Unknown bean / builtin — declare bml:bean Aggregation or use a V1 #built-in.
5. Type / payload mismatch — align expression result with member type; map call args via
   FunctionMapping (doc:FunctionMappingModel).
6. Linking (@bean.capa without parens) — source Outbound, target Inbound, compatible payloads.
7. Relative @model: — ensure a parent Aggregation established binding context.
8. V1 — avoid deferred @bean execution / model / linking features until implemented.
Resolve ${ } and <$ $> expression diagnostics — syntax, unknown refs, type/payload
    mismatches, linking, and model context.
342.idea: A how-to for fixing expression errors

343.name: FixMemberOverride
343.documentation:
Procedure when the validator reports an override/merge-related BML_* code:
1. Determine whether the local member is new or merges with baseType/contracts identity
   (resolvedNamespace + normalizedLogicalName).
2. Merging redeclaration → set override="true" on every layer (including contract completion).
3. New member → do not set override="true".
4. Abstract obligation on a concrete Block → complete locally (type/value/implementation) with
   override="true", or keep abstract="true" on the redeclaration.
5. final or private parent → do not override; change modeling approach.
6. readOnly → set values on definitions/overrides only, not on Block instances.
7. Aggregation fill-only override → omit unchanged type (BML_REDUNDANT_AGGREGATION_TYPE).
Resolve override-required / without-parent, abstract-not-implemented, final override,
    readOnly instance writes, and redundant aggregation type warnings.
343.idea: A how-to for fixing member override errors

344.name: FixTypeIdentity
344.documentation:
Procedure when type identity or reference resolution fails:
1. Classify the Block role — root, Sub-Block, or embedded virtual file.
2. Root — require type; optional name must equal lastSegment(resolve(type)).
3. Sub-Block — require name; omit type or match parentType + "." + name from the immediate
   enclosing block; never declare embeddedBlocks.
4. Embedded — require fully qualified type; FQN is not nested under the root; no nested embeds.
5. Unqualified names — use nested resolution (innermost first) or context-bound implicit
   namespace; grandchildren need a relative path; otherwise qualify with xmlns/FQN.
6. Ambiguous short Sub-Block names that match the root — rename or use qualified references.
Resolve root/Sub-Block/embedded identity mismatches, ambiguous or unqualified references,
    and definition-role errors.
344.idea: A how-to for fixing type identity errors

345.name: FixVisibilityAccess
345.documentation:
Procedure when the validator reports a visibility-related BML_* code:
1. Identify whether the site is a member or a Sub-Block (same naming convention).
2. Confirm the intended visibility via name prefix: public / _protected / __private.
3. For access errors — move the use into an allowed context (declaring Block, inheritance,
   immediate composition owner for protected) or widen the declaration if appropriate.
4. For override narrowing — keep or widen visibility; never narrow; private cannot be overridden.
5. For duplicate variants — keep exactly one normalizedLogicalName with one visibility.
6. For root-level <visibility> on a root Block — remove it (Sub-Blocks only).
Resolve private/protected member or Sub-Block access errors, visibility mismatches,
    narrowing on override, and duplicate visibility-prefix variants.
345.idea: A how-to for fixing visibility errors

346.name: AggregationReference
346.documentation:
Concrete MemberReference binding D = AggregationDefinition. Value is a canonical
    aggregation path (com.foo.Bar.aggregations.children) or a local aggregation name when paired
    with a type qualifier. Used as the type of see aggregation=.
346.idea: A path to an Aggregation member

347.name: AssociationReference
347.documentation:
Concrete MemberReference binding D = AssociationDefinition. Value is a canonical
    association path (com.foo.Bar.associations.basePresets) or a local association name when paired
    with a type qualifier. Used as the type of see association=.
347.idea: A path to an Association member

348.name: Boolean
348.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for true/false values. Unqualified name Boolean
    resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean. Boolean is neither textual nor numeric — its own
    primitive branch. Values are stored in Properties — not on the Boolean type itself.

    Authoring accepts case variants of the literals: true / True / TRUE and false / False / FALSE.
    Preferred form is lowercase true and false. The BOM always stores the canonical boolean
    (lowercase true or false) — never the authored casing.

    Sub-Blocks True and False are Constant(Boolean) singletons — use type:Boolean.True /
    type:Boolean.False (or Boolean.True / Boolean.False) as named alternatives to
    Constant(Boolean){true} / Constant(Boolean){false} in type expressions.

349.fqnText: org blockml bml type Boolean False
349.name: False
349.documentation:
Singleton Constant for the literal false.
        FQN: org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean.False.
        Equivalent to Constant(Boolean){false} / Constant(Boolean){value: false}.

350.fqnText: org blockml bml type Boolean True
350.name: True
350.documentation:
Singleton Constant for the literal true.
        FQN: org.blockml.bml.type.Boolean.True.
        Equivalent to Constant(Boolean){true} / Constant(Boolean){value: true}.

351.name: BooleanEntity
351.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a Boolean primitive. Binds T = Boolean on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
351.idea: A true-or-false value as an Entity

352.name: CapabilityReference
352.documentation:
Concrete MemberReference binding D = CapabilityDefinition. Value is a canonical
    capability path (com.foo.Bar.capabilities.render) or a local capability name when paired with a
    type qualifier. Used as the type of see capability=.
352.idea: A path to a Capability member

353.name: Color
353.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for color values. Unqualified name Color resolves to
    org.blockml.bml.type.Color.

    Accepted forms (case-insensitive for function names and named colors):
    • Hex — CSS lengths #RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA (for example #afafaf, #a3d4e200)
    • rgb / RGB — rgb(255,12,230)
    • rgba / RGBA — rgba(34,54,21,0.5) with alpha in the CSS 0–1 range
    • Named color — free-text name in language L (for example red, Blue); the base Color type
      does not validate named colors against a catalogue. A subtype may later constrain L to a
      fixed set of names.

    Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) names the language of free-text color
    names. Bare Color resolves to English; supply Color(lang:German) only when named colors are
    expected in another language.

354.name: ColorEntity
354.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a Color primitive. Binds T = Color on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
    Bare Color uses L = English for free-text color names.
354.idea: A color value as an Entity

355.name: Constant
355.documentation:
Standard ConstantType implementation for singleton (constant) values in type expressions —
without a dedicated literal-type language feature. Unqualified name Constant resolves to
org.blockml.bml.type.Constant.

Constant(T) binds the generic parameter T to any ValueType. Instance configuration supplies
the single allowed value via the value Property — for example Constant(Text){value: "auto"} or
Constant(Integer){value: 5}. The generic type argument is mandatory; bare Constant or
Constant{value: "auto"} without (T) is invalid.

The configured value Property belongs to the internal ValueType instance on the Property
definition. The external representation is always identical to the representation of the
underlying generic type T — Constant(Text){value: "auto"} accepts the external value "auto",
not { value: "auto" }.

Validation proceeds in two steps: first against the bound type T, then equality with the
configured constant value. No type inference is required — T is always authored explicitly
at the reference site.

Used primarily as a union alternative alongside ordinary ValueTypes:

Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

Future literal union syntax (Boolean | "auto") desugars to this form. See
doc:ConstantValueType.

356.name: ConstantType
356.documentation:
Abstract ValueType branch for constant (singleton) value types. Unqualified name ConstantType
resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.ConstantType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). ConstantType is neither a PrimitiveType, StructType, nor EnumType:

• A PrimitiveType defines a value domain (Text → all text values; Integer → all integers).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; BOM stores id + typeFqn only.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain — a value is valid if and only if it
  conforms to the underlying generic ValueType and equals the configured constant value.

The standard implementation is Constant<T extends ValueType> with a single Property
value : T. The generic type parameter is mandatory. Instance configuration supplies the
allowed value — for example Constant(Text){value: "auto"} or Constant(Integer){value: 5}.

The configured value Property belongs to the internal ValueType instance on the Property
definition — not to the property's external representation. The external value is always
identical to the representation of the underlying generic type T. For
Constant(Text){value: "auto"}, the external value is "auto" — not { value: "auto" }.

Validation proceeds in two steps:
1. Validate the supplied value against the generic ValueType T.
2. Compare the supplied value with the configured constant value.

Used primarily as a union alternative alongside ordinary ValueTypes:

Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

357.name: Decimal
357.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for decimal numbers — the default type for all
    non-integer numeric values (3.5, 12.75, 0.1). Unqualified name Decimal resolves to
    org.blockml.bml.type.Decimal. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Represents mathematical decimal
    numbers; the renderer decides target representation (BigDecimal, decimal, number, …).
    Payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Decimal type itself.

    Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
    Decimal(unit:Meter). Bare Decimal is dimensionless.

    Optional configuration Properties (precision, scale) configure a Property's owned Decimal
    instance via inline type syntax — Decimal{precision: 10, scale: 2} or Decimal{10, 2}.
    Positional order: precision, scale. See 20_value_type_instance_configuration.md.

358.name: DecimalEntity
358.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a Decimal primitive. Binds T = Decimal on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
358.idea: A decimal number as an Entity

359.name: EnumType
359.documentation:
Abstract ValueType branch for closed enum ValueTypes — finite sets of named literal values.
Unqualified name EnumType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.EnumType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). EnumType is its own ValueType branch — not a StructType and not a
PrimitiveType:

• A PrimitiveType defines an open value domain (Text → all text values).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; the external property value is the
  member identity (id + EnumType), not a struct payload.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain.

Concrete EnumTypes declare allowed members as Block instances in the default values
aggregation — no special enum syntax. Examples: Direction, Face, StudType, BaseCutout,
Align.

Each catalog member is a Block instance of the EnumType with a mandatory bml:id (the
reference token). An EnumType may declare arbitrary properties on the type — filled per
member in values — analogous to private fields on a Java enum constant. Those properties
are catalog metadata on the type definition (for example a MachineBlocks value string for
SCAD). They are not part of the stored property value when an EnumType is used.

BOM storage for a property typed with an EnumType is only id + typeFqn (the EnumType).
Catalog properties are looked up from the EnumType definition when a renderer or tool needs
them. The editor renders EnumType properties as a SelectBox; the compiler validates authored
tokens against values by id.

Properties typed with an EnumType must not carry <suggestions> — valid values come
exclusively from values → BML_SUGGESTIONS_ON_ENUM. Properties may still carry
<constraints> where a compatible Constraint sub-type exists.

Enum value references in property values (defaultValue, composition attributes, expressions):
when the property type is an EnumType, qualified references may omit the {EnumTypeFQN}::
prefix — Standard is equivalent to com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout::Standard when the
expected type is known from the property declaration. The short form is invalid for untyped
strings. The validator resolves tokens against values by id; unknown values → validation
error.

Domain XSD enums remain accepted during migration with BML_LEGACY_TYPE_SOURCE warning — new
enums should be defined as BML EnumType blocks.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates closed value sets:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout")
• defaultValue and instance attribute values on EnumType properties
• Expression enum literals where the expected EnumType is known from context
• Library blocks export alongside other ValueType definitions
359.idea: A closed set of named values

360.name: FilePath
360.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for file path values. Unqualified name FilePath resolves
    to org.blockml.bml.type.FilePath.

361.name: FilePathEntity
361.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a FilePath primitive. Binds T = FilePath on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
361.idea: A filesystem path as an Entity

362.name: Float
362.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for binary floating-point numbers. Not the default
    floating-point type — use Decimal unless binary IEEE754 semantics are explicitly required
    (GPU, OpenGL, native C APIs, binary protocols). Unqualified name Float resolves to
    org.blockml.bml.type.Float. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Values are stored in Properties.

    Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
    Float(unit:Millimeter). Bare Float is dimensionless.

363.name: FloatEntity
363.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a Float primitive. Binds T = Float on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
363.idea: A floating-point number as an Entity

364.name: InstanceReference
364.documentation:
ValueType for non-owning pointers to concrete Block instances identified by bml:id.
Unqualified name InstanceReference resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.InstanceReference.

Lexical forms:
• Local id — myId (visibility-scoped within the enclosing composition)
• Qualified — {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{instanceId} (e.g. com.foo.Bar::myId)
• Prefixed qualified — foo:Bar::myId (xmlns QName of the enclosing Block document, then :: and id)

Not a Block type FQN (use TypeReference), not a member definition path (use MemberReference /
AssociationReference), and not a resource URI (use URI).

Generic parameter:
• T (baseType core:Block) — target instance must satisfy T

In type="..." attributes, write generic applications with round parentheses:
• InstanceReference(core:Block) → 0..1 pointer to a core:Block instance
• InstanceReference(bml:Self)[] → 0..n pointers to instances of the effective Block type

Primary use — AssociationDefinition type (associations may only declare InstanceReference(T)
or InstanceReference(T)[] — instance-to-instance model links). Also the type of see instance=
on StructuralDefinition.Reference (documentation type→instance links — not Associations).

Resolution and visibility rules: docs/01_bom_core.md — Qualified Block Instance References
(public aggregation, static authored bml:id, BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF, …).

365.name: Integer
365.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for whole numbers. Unqualified name Integer resolves
    to org.blockml.bml.type.Integer. Extends org.blockml.bml.type.Number. Payload values are stored on
    Properties — not on the Integer type itself.

    Generic parameter N (Unit, default unit:None) is forwarded from Number — e.g.
    Integer(unit:Millimeter). Bare Integer is dimensionless.

    Optional configuration Properties (min, max) configure a Property's owned Integer instance via
    inline type syntax — Integer{min: 0, max: 100}. Positional order: min, max. See
    20_value_type_instance_configuration.md.

366.name: IntegerEntity
366.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping an Integer primitive. Binds T = Integer on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
    Use when an integer must appear as an identifiable Block instance.
366.idea: A whole number as an Entity

367.name: MemberReference
367.documentation:
Abstract ValueType for references to Block member definitions — properties,
    aggregations, associations, and capabilities. Extends TypeReference(B); adds D to constrain
    which MemberDefinition branch the path may target.

    Value forms:
    • Canonical definition path — for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width
    • Local member name when paired with a type qualifier (for example see type="com.foo.Bar"
      property="width" → com.foo.Bar.properties.width)

    Generic parameters:
    • B (from TypeReference) — owning Block branch for the member's enclosing type
    • D (baseType def:MemberDefinition) — member definition kind constraint

    Concrete specializations bind D:
    • PropertyReference     → D = def:PropertyDefinition
    • AggregationReference  → D = def:AggregationDefinition
    • AssociationReference  → D = def:AssociationDefinition
    • CapabilityReference   → D = def:CapabilityDefinition

    Primary use — StructuralDefinition Reference (see) member target attributes. Not for Block type
    identity (use TypeReference), instance pointers (use InstanceReference), or type-reference
    aggregations (use TypeReferenceEntity).
367.idea: A path to a Block member

368.name: MimeType
368.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for MIME type values (for example text/plain,
    application/json). Unqualified name MimeType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.MimeType.

369.name: MimeTypeEntity
369.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a MimeType primitive. Binds T = MimeType on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
369.idea: A MIME type as an Entity

370.name: Number
370.documentation:
Abstract numeric primitive branch under org.blockml.bml.type.PrimitiveType.
    Concrete types: Integer (whole numbers), Decimal (default for non-integer numeric values),
    Float (binary floating-point — only when IEEE754 semantics are explicitly required).
    Abstract numeric branch — not resolvable via Property.type implicit namespace; use Integer, Decimal, or Float explicitly.
    Numeric types describe semantics only; values are stored in Properties.

    Generic parameter N constrains the measurement unit (extends org.blockml.bml.core.Unit).
    Default is org.blockml.bml.unit.None — bare Number / Integer / Decimal / Float are dimensionless.
    Supply N at reference sites when a unit is required, e.g. Integer(unit:Millimeter).

371.name: PrimitiveType
371.documentation:
Abstract branch for built-in scalar ValueTypes. PrimitiveTypes describe semantics
    only — they never store concrete values. All values are stored exclusively in Properties.

    Numeric branch: Number (Integer, Decimal, Float). Textual branch: Text (TypeReference,
    MemberReference / PropertyReference / …, Version, URL, URI, FilePath, MimeType, …). Boolean is
    its own branch — neither textual nor numeric.

    When a primitive value must exist as an Entity inside a composition or aggregation, use a
    concrete Entity specialization (for example IntegerEntity) — not by adding a value member to
    the PrimitiveType.

    Invalid: <type:Integer value="5"/> — PrimitiveTypes cannot carry values.
    Valid: <property name="count" type="Integer"><value>5</value></property>

372.name: PropertyReference
372.documentation:
Concrete MemberReference binding D = PropertyDefinition. Value is a canonical
    property path (com.foo.Bar.properties.width) or a local property name when paired with a Block
    qualifier. Used as the type of see property= and other PropertyDefinition reference sites.
372.idea: A path to a Property member

373.name: StructType
373.documentation:
Abstract ValueType branch for composite value objects — complex values described by normal
Properties. Unqualified name StructType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.StructType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). StructType is a dedicated branch — EnumType is a sibling under ValueType,
not a subtype of StructType.
StructTypes describe the structure of a value — their properties define the data layout.
StructTypes usually contain no values themselves; Property values remain stored in the owning
Property. Default values on StructType property definitions are allowed. Concrete StructTypes
declare <properties> whose members become struct fields — no special struct syntax.
Examples: Size3d, Color, Address, Transform. Parameterized value types (for example Box<T>)
are StructTypes that declare <genericTypes> — not a separate ValueType branch.

Struct property access is exclusively by name (size.x, size.y, size.z). Numeric index access
on StructType members (size[0]) is not valid — StructType is a typed object with named
properties only. Positional function-parameter syntax (#tool.capa("x", "y")) is handled by
FunctionMapping at call sites, not by general StructType semantics.

Field declaration order remains significant for:
• Positional array literals (size="[4, 2, 3]") — values map to properties by declaration order
• FunctionMapping positional parameter order for capability calls
• Compatibility — existing field order must not change across versions; new fields may be
  appended only at the end

Named object literals (size="{ x: 4, y: 2, z: 3 }") and attribute syntax on StructType
instances (<Size3d x="4" y="2" z="3"/>) are type-equivalent authoring forms.

Anonymous StructTypes — { field: Type, … } is a StructType without a declared name, written
directly in a type expression; it is the mechanism for structured Capability inputs. Each field
is Identifier ":" TypeExpression, so a field type is a full type expression and not merely an
unqualified type name: qualified references, multiplicity, generics, unions, instance
configuration, and nested anonymous StructTypes are all valid.
• { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } — qualified reference with multiplicity
• { values: foo:Thing[1..n] } · { value: Integer | Text } · { nested: { x: Integer, y: Integer } }
The field-name separator and the prefix colon of a qualified reference sit at different grammar
levels (list : core:ValueType[]) — unambiguous, not a naming conflict. Field declaration order is
significant exactly as for named StructTypes. Rejecting a qualified field type while accepting an
unqualified one is a parser / mapper limitation, not a type-expression ambiguity.
See doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates structured values:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.Size3d")
• Block instances of the StructType as composition children or property payloads
• Capability inputType / outputType — named StructType or anonymous struct expressions
• Generic type applications (for example Box<Integer>) on StructTypes with
  <genericTypes>

374.name: Text
374.documentation:
BOM Core primitive ValueType for text. Unqualified name Text resolves to
    org.blockml.bml.type.Text. Replaces the former String type — BlockML describes semantic types, not
    implementation data structures. Renderers may map Text to Java String, TypeScript string,
    Python str, C# string, or any target representation.

    Semantic subtypes extend Text: TypeReference (and MemberReference / PropertyReference / …),
    Version, URL, URI, FilePath, MimeType, …
    Concrete payload values are stored on Properties — not on the Text type itself.

    Optional configuration Properties (minLength, maxLength) configure a Property's owned Text
    instance via inline type syntax — Text{maxLength: 100}. Positional order: minLength, maxLength.
    See 20_value_type_instance_configuration.md.

375.name: TextEntity
375.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a Text primitive. Binds T = Text on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
375.idea: A text string as an Entity

376.name: TypeReference
376.documentation:
ValueType for type references — fully qualified names (FQNs) and TypeExpressions that name a
Block. Unqualified name TypeReference resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.TypeReference. Formerly
FullyQualifiedName; the FQN string format is unchanged.

FQN format (Java-style reverse-domain, dot-separated):
• Package segments — lowercase, reverse-domain (for example org.blockml.bml.core,
  com.machineblocks.bml.type)
• Class segment — PascalCase (for example Block, Integer, Wall)
• Full form — <package>.<ClassName> (for example org.blockml.bml.type.Integer,
  com.machineblocks.bml.core.Block)
Sub-Block FQNs derive as parentFqn + "." + name when omitted in source.

Namespace prefixes in BML (core:, type:, def:, …) map to package segments; the Namespace
Resolver stores the resolved FQN string in BOM typeFqn fields. Unknown FQN at validate time
→ BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE.

Generic parameter:
• B (baseType core:Block) — Block branch constraint for the referenced type

In type="..." attributes, write generic applications with round parentheses — not angle
brackets (XML-safe, readable):
• TypeReference(core:Block) → B = core.Block
• TypeReference(core:Language) → B = core.Language

Concrete type arguments must satisfy B's baseType constraint → BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

Primary use — Block-definition identity (`type`, `baseType`) and definition metadata where a
type attribute or property holds a Block FQN / TypeExpression string. When a type reference must
appear as an Entity in composition or aggregation, use org.blockml.bml.type.TypeReferenceEntity.

Instance pointers (bml:id / FQN::id) use org.blockml.bml.type.InstanceReference — not
TypeReference. Member definition paths (property, aggregation, association, capability) use the
org.blockml.bml.type.MemberReference branch — not TypeReference.

377.name: TypeReferenceEntity
377.documentation:
Open generic Entity wrapping a TypeReference (FQN / TypeExpression) primitive.
    Forwards B from org.blockml.bml.type.TypeReference onto org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via
    baseType — inherits the value property automatically as value : TypeReference(B).

    Use on aggregation type attributes when children are type references stored as Entity instances:
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Block)[] — contracts, Library blocks
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Group)[] — StructuralDefinition.groups (narrowed on subtypes)
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(group:MemberGroup)[] — MemberDefinition.groups
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(group:BlockGroup)[] — BlockDefinition.groups
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(lang:NaturalLanguage) — language (singular, 0..1)
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:ReadMe)[1..1] — Library readMe
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:Bootstrap) — Library bootstrap (0..1 SPOE)
    • type:TypeReferenceEntity(core:BlockLibrary)[] — dependencies, subLibraries

    Authored empty child whose element QName is not TypeReferenceEntity is syntactic sugar for a
    TypeReferenceEntity instance with value set to that QName (resolved to FQN) — for example
    <foo:Bar /> expands to <type:TypeReferenceEntity value="foo:Bar" /> (B bound by the
    aggregation type). Optional bml:version on the sugar child is an exact-version assert against
    the referenced type (value), not against TypeReferenceEntity itself — e.g.
    <blockml:Library bml:version="3.0.0" />. Explicit TypeReferenceEntity authoring is always
    valid and equivalent.

    Contrast with scalar TypeReference(B) on properties (identity type / baseType, member type
    attributes) — those remain plain text, not Entity instances. Member path references use
    MemberReference / PropertyReference / … — not this Entity.

    Replaces the former abstract org.blockml.bml.core.TypeReference aggregation marker and
    FullyQualifiedNameEntity.
377.idea: A type name reference as an Entity

378.name: URI
378.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for URI values. Unqualified name URI resolves to
    org.blockml.bml.type.URI.

379.name: URIEntity
379.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a URI primitive. Binds T = URI on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
379.idea: A resource identifier as an Entity

380.name: URL
380.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for URL values. Unqualified name URL resolves to
    org.blockml.bml.type.URL.

381.name: URLEntity
381.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a URL primitive. Binds T = URL on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
381.idea: A web address as an Entity

382.name: Version
382.documentation:
Textual primitive subtype for semantic version numbers (semver). Values use
    MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH form (for example 1.0.0, 1.3.2). Unqualified name Version resolves to
    org.blockml.bml.type.Version.

    Used wherever BlockML tracks or compares definition and reference versions: <version> on
    Block and Library definitions, <since> on members, changelog entries, and bml:version on
    composition instances. Concrete version strings are stored in Properties — not on the Version
    type itself.

383.name: VersionEntity
383.documentation:
Concrete Entity wrapping a Version primitive. Binds T = Version on
    org.blockml.bml.core.PrimitiveEntity via baseType — inherits the value property automatically.
383.idea: A version number as an Entity

385.name: Degree
385.documentation:
Angular unit — degree of arc (°). Use for rotation and orientation angles,
    e.g. Decimal(unit:Degree) or Float(unit:Degree).

389.name: None
389.documentation: Dimensionless Unit — use when a value has no associated unit of measure.

390.name: Error
390.documentation:
When a constraint with validation="Error" is violated, the BlockML
    validator emits BML_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION and compilation fails.

391.name: Information
391.documentation:
When a constraint with validation="Information" is violated, the BlockML
    validator emits BML_CONSTRAINT_INFORMATION. Compilation continues.

392.name: Warning
392.documentation:
When a constraint with validation="Warning" is violated, the BlockML
    validator emits BML_CONSTRAINT_WARNING. Compilation continues.

<composition> must always be nested inside an aggregation member on Block definitions. On instances, open aggregations directly without a composition wrapper. Do not use <value> as a parallel wrapper on instance Properties — both are definition fields (doc:MemberAuthoring).
Emitted when <composition> appears outside an aggregation member element.

<name> is a class name — PascalCase, letters and digits only:

Format: [A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*
Valid: Wall, StandardBrick, Calibrator, NfcPlayer
Invalid: my-wall, wall_v2, 2Wall, My Wall
Error: BML_INVALID_BLOCK_NAME

PascalCase ensures composition instance tags with xmlns prefixes are unambiguous — no Property
or member name starts with an uppercase letter (members use camelCase; visibility prefixes _ /
__ do not change that rule for the logical name).

Relationship to type identity (doc:TypeIdentityDerivation):
• Root Blocks — type is canonical; name is optional and must equal lastSegment(resolve(type))
  when present (BML_BLOCK_NAME_TYPE_MISMATCH)
• Sub-Blocks — name is required local identity; type is normally derived as
  parentType + "." + name
• Visibility prefixes on Sub-Block names (_Utils, __Helper) are allowed; the PascalCase rule
  applies to the logical name after stripping visibility prefixes for collision checks — authored
  names still follow the visibility naming convention (doc:MemberVisibility /
  doc:SubBlockModel)

Prefer distinctive Sub-Block names that differ from the enclosing root Block name to avoid
ambiguous short tags (doc:SubBlockModel — naming vs parent).

A Composition fills an Aggregation with concrete child Block instances. On Block definitions,
<composition> is nested inside the aggregation member. On Block instances, aggregations are
filled directly by member name — no <composition> wrapper. Do not treat composition as a
general-purpose container; the parallel Property mistake is wrapping instance values in
<value> — both are definition fields, not instance wrappers (doc:MemberAuthoring). The
composition aggregation="…" attribute is removed.

Unified container concept — one idea, two forms:
• composition — initial fill of an aggregation inside a Block definition only
• bml:container — general virtual container everywhere else (Block instances)
Both support the same flow-control directives: bml:if, bml:each, bml:with (and future container
directives). See doc:BmlDirectives.

Placement rules:
• <composition> must always be nested inside an aggregation member — never standalone →
  BML_STANDALONE_COMPOSITION
• New aggregation declaration → type required
• Inherited aggregation override → override="true" required; type may be omitted (identical
  restated type → BML_REDUNDANT_AGGREGATION_TYPE)
• Block instances open aggregations directly — recursive nested structure is first-class

Child elements inside composition (or instance aggregation content) are Block instances:
• Tag name — Block type (FQN / xmlns QName)
• bml:id — composition instance identity; required when referenced or on bml:each (literal or
  Expression). Omitted on anonymous static children → auto-ID after directive expansion
• bml:version — optional exact-version assert on external type references; omitted → TypeRegistry
  / library context; no match → BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION. Same-document Sub-Block refs omit version
• bml:bean / bml:scope — optional service bean registration (local | context; default local)
• Member attributes / child elements — property and nested aggregation values (literals or
  ${ … } expressions)

Instance ID reachability is controlled by the aggregation member's visibility — not by flags on
composition or bml:container. Public aggregations export ids for cross-document
{EnclosingBlockFQN}::{id}; protected and private narrow reach as in doc:MemberVisibility.
Qualified cross-document references require a public target aggregation and a literal static
bml:id.

Recursive composition: every Block instance may contain aggregation members directly — complex
object structures nest wherever instances appear.

Sibling value sharing: use bml:with on a common ancestor (composition or bml:container). Variables
are visible to the element and all descendants — no separate registry. Full expression grammar
lives in doc:Expressions; V1 implements property references, #built-in calls, and bml: directives
(including bml:with). @bean / @model: / capability linking are specified but not V1-implemented.

Meta-model: AggregationDefinition.composition (Sub-Block Composition) maps to BOM
CompositionTemplate. Service binding uses bml:bean and bml:scope on instances — not aggregation
member fields.

A genuinely new member must not set override="true". Check namespace + normalizedLogicalName identity and contract merge order.
Emitted when override="true" is set but no matching parent member exists in the baseType chain or contracts[].

A Library groups related Block and ValueType definitions into a publishable unit. Concrete
libraries use name Library, filename Library.bml, baseType org.blockml.bml.core.BlockLibrary.
FQN = {package}.Library from the file's package path.

Membership is defined exclusively by Library.bml blocks — not by directory layout. A .bml
file is a library member only if listed in that library's blocks. Without a Library block,
all .bml source files in the directory are public.

Structure (catalog aggregations are public and readOnly — inspectable from foreign Blocks;
authored only on the Library definition):
• readMe — required human/LLM reading entry (ReadMe, 1..1; typically README)
• bootstrap — optional automation SPOE (Bootstrap, 0..1)
• dependencies — other Library blocks (typical: inner library depends on outer)
• subLibraries — nested child Library blocks grouped under this library
• blocks — exported Block and ValueType definitions
• schemas — optional legacy XSD paths as FilePathEntity instances during migration
• version on Library.bml — framework convention: version only on Library for org.blockml.bml.*

Concrete Library.bml <references> — at most two <see> entries:
1. Required relation=ReadFirst → the ReadMe named in readMe
2. Optional relation=ThenContinueWith → the Bootstrap named in bootstrap (only when present)
No other relations on the catalog descriptor; deep links belong on documentation blocks.

Nested libraries may coexist at different package levels (org.blockml.bml.Library and
org.blockml.bml.compiler.Library are separate units). Typical pattern: inner library lists
outer in dependencies; outer lists inner in subLibraries. Violation: outer blocks
referencing a Block exported by an inner library → BML_LIBRARY_NESTING_VIOLATION.

Namespaces: xmlns prefixes map to FQN package prefixes. BOM stores canonical FQNs only —
prefixes are authoring convenience. Every BML definition must reside under
<domain>.bml.* — no Block, Library, or other BlockML definition may exist outside
the domain's bml namespace. See doc:BmlNamespace.

Version resolution:
effectiveBlockVersion = own version if present, else library.version if exported via blocks,
else error BML_MISSING_VERSION. bml:version on TypeReferenceEntity sugar (readMe, bootstrap,
dependencies, subLibraries, blocks) is an optional exact-version assert against the referenced
type (value); omitted → TypeRegistry / library context; no match → BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION.

Abstract base for all annotation directives. The name property is the
        directive local name under the annotation namespace (e.g. id, with, document, examples,
        example, value). Member directives fix name to "*"; Document, Summary, Examples, Example,
        and Value fix document / summary / examples / example / value; Attribute and Element
        concretes set an explicit local name.

Abstract base for Block and member definitions that support a <constraints>
    container. The embedding context determines the constraint target and binds the generic type
    parameter automatically — no target property in BML. Validator checks branch compatibility via
    the constraint baseType chain (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH). Constraint order in BML is
    preserved in BOM. Target binding and generic resolution are not stored in the Canonical BOM.

Abstract base for org.blockml.bml.documentation.* blocks — curated reading material that
explains BlockML concepts in mental learning order. Each concrete documentation block
carries is, documentation, and references; cross-links belong in references, not in
documentation prose. Listed via relation=ReadFirst on README and other ReadMe blocks.
Procedural how-to blocks extend org.blockml.bml.core.TaskGuide instead.

Abstract base type for Block member declarations — properties, aggregations,
    associations, and capabilities. Rendered as a child element inside the corresponding member
    container on BlockDefinition; the XML element name is the member name (bml:xml="${ #this.name }").
    An optional XML prefix on the element name supplies the member namespace — resolved via xmlns to
    BOM namespace; unprefixed elements use the default namespace (empty string). Member identity is
    (resolvedNamespace, normalizedLogicalName) — visibility prefixes (_ / __) are stripped from the
    element localName before match or collision checks. Declaration properties abstract, final, and
    override are local to each member declaration — not inherited. Only their semantic effects
    propagate (implementation obligations, override prohibitions).

    Member value placement (scalar members on PropertyDefinition, CapabilityDefinition, and shared
    MemberDefinition fields):
    • On member declarations (Block definition documents): each declaration field may render as a
      child element or as an attribute on the member element — both are valid; element form is
      preferred when serializing definitions (e.g. <type>Integer</type> over
      type="Integer"; <value>…</value> over value="…").
    • On Block instances (composition): the member itself renders as an attribute or child element
      of the Block — both are valid; attribute form is preferred (e.g. width="50" over
      <width>50</width>). Do not wrap the payload in <value> or <composition>
      — those are PropertyDefinition / AggregationDefinition declaration fields only. Exception: a
      member whose name is value uses value="…" / <value> as the member itself. See
      doc:MemberAuthoring.
    Structured children (constraints, groups, suggestions, composition, implementation) remain
    elements.

    Member declaration modes are orthogonal:
    • new — introduces a new member; must not set override="true"
    • override="true" — refines an inherited member of the same identity (namespace +
      normalizedLogicalName). Required on every local redeclaration that merges with an existing
      member from the baseType chain or from contracts[] — including contract member completion. Each
      redeclaration layer must set override="true" again — override is not inherited. Omission when a
      parent member exists → BML_OVERRIDE_REQUIRED. Visibility may widen on override (e.g. protected
      `_name` → public `name`); narrowing → BML_VISIBILITY_NARROWING. Member-level bml:xml may change
      on the same override. Private members cannot be overridden → BML_FINAL_MEMBER_OVERRIDE.

    Declaration properties abstract, final, and override are boolean properties local to the current
    declaration (default false). They are never inherited; only semantic effects apply across layers:
    - abstract="true" creates an implementation obligation for concrete descendants
    - final="true" prevents redeclaration in child blocks (validator checks all declaring layers)
    - override="true" confirms a deliberate redefinition of an inherited member

    A locally concrete redeclaration (abstract=false, the default) with override="true" satisfies an
    inherited implementation obligation when it is complete for the member kind (Property: type;
    Aggregation: type; Association: type; Capability: type + implementation). To keep a member
    abstract in a child block, explicitly declare abstract="true" on that redeclaration.

    Maps to BOM MemberDefinitionBase fields shared by all member kinds — including visibility and
    readOnly attributes, plus the groups aggregation (MemberGroup type references).

Abstract base type for BlockML structural definition elements. It provides the common
documentation model consisting of summaries[], keywords, groups, documentations[] (i18n via
language= and optional QName facets — facets are not for locales), version information, change
history, examples, and references, plus local declaration properties (abstract, final) for block
definitions. Concrete structural definition types inherit these members to describe themselves
consistently. Member declarations declare abstract, final, and override locally via
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition. BlockDefinition and MemberDefinition override
groups to narrow the Group branch (BlockGroup and MemberGroup respectively).

Abstract base type for groups — named categories that organize related elements
    for editors and tooling. Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks.
    Concrete group kinds extend this branch (e.g. org.blockml.bml.group.MemberGroup for Block
    members, org.blockml.bml.group.BlockGroup for Blocks).

Abstract Block branch for measurement units — a taxonomy/catalog like Language
    or Status, not a ValueType. Unit blocks describe a unit of measure; they never store concrete
    magnitudes and are not valid as Property type or Capability inputType/outputType. They appear
    as generic type arguments on Number (and domain types such as MultiAxis) — e.g.
    Decimal(unit:Millimeter), Float(unit:Degree). Standard implementations live in
    org.blockml.bml.unit.*; domain libraries may define additional unit blocks.

Abstract branch for annotation namespaces. Every BML-semantic xmlns prefix must resolve to
either a Package (FQN prefix under which types live) or a concrete Annotation. Annotations are
orthogonal to the Definition meta-model (org.blockml.bml.definition.*): they do not describe
block structure, members, or constraints. They declare which directive QNames are legal under
a preferred authoring alias (e.g. bml, scad).

preferredAlias is authoring convention only — the BOM stores the Annotation FQN, never the
XML prefix. directives lists the concrete Directive kinds this annotation exposes.

Directive taxonomy (SubBlocks — not Definition member kinds):
• Directive — base; property name is the directive local name
• Member (name="*") — wildcard member directives under this namespace
  → Property · Aggregation · Association · Capability
• Element — element-form directives
  → Document (name="document") · Summary (name="summary") · Examples (name="examples")
    · Example (name="example") — sibling under StructuralDefinition examples container
    · Value (name="value") — PropertyDefinition value-field facets
• Attribute — attribute-form directives (id, with, each, …)

Naming overlap with Definition (Property, Aggregation, …) is classification of directive form
only — Annotation.Property is not def:PropertyDefinition. Annotation.Value facets nested under
a property declaration (e.g. <myProp><scad:value>…</scad:value></myProp>)
are not the same as a member QName <scad:value/> under <properties> — parent
context disambiguates.

Abstract branch for Block-level structural constraints. May express cross-member
    rules (RequiresMember, MutuallyExclusive, …). Generic T binds to the effective
    org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition type of the enclosing Block (including
    SubBlockDefinition, RootBlockDefinition, and EmbeddedBlockDefinition subtypes). Valid only under a Block's
    <constraints> container (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).

Abstract branch for built-in scalar ValueTypes. PrimitiveTypes describe semantics
    only — they never store concrete values. All values are stored exclusively in Properties.

    Numeric branch: Number (Integer, Decimal, Float). Textual branch: Text (TypeReference,
    MemberReference / PropertyReference / …, Version, URL, URI, FilePath, MimeType, …). Boolean is
    its own branch — neither textual nor numeric.

    When a primitive value must exist as an Entity inside a composition or aggregation, use a
    concrete Entity specialization (for example IntegerEntity) — not by adding a value member to
    the PrimitiveType.

    Invalid: <type:Integer value="5"/> — PrimitiveTypes cannot carry values.
    Valid: <property name="count" type="Integer"><value>5</value></property>

Abstract branch for constraints on Aggregation members. Generic T binds to the
    effective AggregationDefinition. Valid only under an Aggregation's <constraints> container
    (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).

Abstract branch for constraints on Association members. Generic T binds to the
    effective AssociationDefinition. Valid only under an Association's <constraints> container
    (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).

Abstract branch for constraints on Capability members. Generic T binds to the
    effective CapabilityDefinition. Valid only under a Capability's <constraints> container
    (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise).

Abstract branch for constraints on Property definitions (not property values —
    see ValueConstraint for value rules). Generic T binds to the effective PropertyDefinition of
    the enclosing Property. Valid only under a Property's <constraints> container when the
    constraint extends PropertyConstraint (not ValueConstraint).

Abstract branch for Entities — Blocks that represent instances with identity in
    composition or aggregation. Domain blocks, built-in services, and PrimitiveEntity wrappers extend
    Entity. Entity is not a ValueType; use Property with a ValueType for typed payloads.

Abstract branch for explicit value mapping between representations. Mapping is not a property
of StructType — it belongs at the site where a function-like representation is used.

Concrete mappings extend this branch and declare how authored syntax maps to BlockML types and
how BlockML types map to target-language signatures.

Component responsibilities:
• Parser — stores authored syntax only; no mapping in Canonical BOM
• Expression parser — AST with positional, named, object, and array literal arguments
• Validator — resolves capability, selects FunctionMapping, validates mapped input against
  inputType
• Renderer — may emit authored form, evaluate FunctionMapping, or interpret mapping for the
  target system; Canonical BOM stays unchanged

Abstract branch for markup languages — XML and other structured document formats
    used as capability implementation bodies and, for Markdown, as documentation prose. Generic
    parameter L (NaturalLanguage, default English) names the content/text language inside the markup
    (element text, comments, human-facing labels, prose).

    Concrete sub-types forward L via baseType MarkupLanguage(L) and redeclare it locally, so the
    parameter stays open on the sub-type — Markdown(German) is authorable and Markdown(NaturalLanguage)
    is usable as a type bound. Because L defaults to English, a bare sub-type name needs no argument:
    Markdown ≡ Markdown(English). Binding L in baseType instead (MarkupLanguage(lang:German)) fixes
    the content language for that sub-type and closes the parameter.

Abstract branch for member-level structural constraints. Generic T binds to the
    effective MemberDefinition subtype of the embedding context. Specialized by PropertyConstraint,
    AggregationConstraint, AssociationConstraint, and CapabilityConstraint.

Abstract branch for natural languages used in documentation text, example
    titles, and natural-language capability implementations. All locale-specific language blocks
    (English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, …) must extend this branch —
    not org.blockml.bml.core.Language directly. Distinct from implementation languages
    (ProgrammingLanguage, MarkupLanguage) used in capability bodies and example content. Those
    formal branches reuse NaturalLanguage as optional generic L (default English) when their
    content/text language must be named.

Abstract branch for org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* blocks. Each concrete diagnostic
    block documents one validator or parser code (for example BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE) with is, summary,
    keywords, and references. Use relation=Resolves on <see> to link to a TaskGuide that
    walks through the fix. Enables agents and humans to navigate from a reported error to a
    procedural resolution path without searching documentation prose.

Abstract branch for org.blockml.bml.task.* blocks — step-by-step procedures
    distinct from org.blockml.bml.documentation.* concept blocks. TaskGuide blocks carry the normal
    documentation model (is, summary, keywords, documentation, references). Ordered procedure
    steps use relation=TaskStep on <see> entries; prerequisites use relation=Prerequisite.
    Task catalogs on README / ReadMe blocks list available tasks via relation=TaskIndex.
    Tooling filters by relation to build learn paths (ReadFirst), task paths (TaskStep), or error
    fix paths (Diagnostic blocks with relation=Resolves).

Abstract branch for programming languages — TypeScript, OpenSCAD, PseudoCode, and
    other languages with defined or interpretable syntax. Generic parameter L (NaturalLanguage,
    default English) names the content/text language of the formal code — for example pseudocode
    prose, identifiers, or LLM-oriented wording.

    Concrete sub-types forward L via baseType ProgrammingLanguage(L) and redeclare it locally, so the
    parameter stays open on the sub-type — PseudoCode(German) is authorable and
    PseudoCode(NaturalLanguage) is usable as a type bound. Because L defaults to English, a bare
    sub-type name needs no argument: TypeScript ≡ TypeScript(English). Binding L in baseType instead
    (ProgrammingLanguage(lang:German)) fixes the content language for that sub-type and closes the
    parameter.

Abstract branch for ReadMe blocks. A ReadMe declares where humans and LLMs start
    reading a library — curated learning order, vocabulary, and orientation. Distinct from
    org.blockml.bml.core.Bootstrap, which is the optional single point of entry (SPOE) for automated
    startup (tasks, agents, CI pipelines).

    org.blockml.bml.README is the standard ReadMe for the core library. Library descriptors point
    here via the required readMe aggregation (1..1).

    ReadMe blocks carry the normal documentation model (is, documentation, references). Curated
    reading order is expressed via <references> with relation=ReadFirst; available task
    catalog entries via relation=TaskIndex — not via separate aggregations on ReadMe itself. The
    abstract base declares no members.

Abstract branch for relation blocks on <see> entries in <references>.
    Relation values are Block references following the Everything-is-a-Block principle.
    Standard implementations live in org.blockml.bml.relation.*; domain libraries may define
    additional relation blocks. Implicit default when omitted on <see>:
    org.blockml.bml.relation.SeeAlso. Standard relations include ReadFirst (README learning path),
    ReadNext (forward edge between documentation blocks), ThenContinueWith (Library bootstrap after
    reading — TypeRelation(core:Bootstrap)), TaskIndex (task catalog), TaskStep and Prerequisite
    (procedural guides), and Resolves (diagnostic to fix task). Unqualified names on relation=
    resolve via implicit namespace org.blockml.bml.relation.*.

    TypeRelation is the constrained subtype for relations that may only target see type= and whose
    target must satisfy a generic Block branch T (default core:Block).

Abstract branch for status blocks. Status values are Block references following the
    Everything-is-a-Block principle. Standard implementations live in org.blockml.bml.status.*;
    domain libraries may define additional status blocks. Implicit default when omitted:
    org.blockml.bml.status.Stable. Status is inherited downward — declare <status> or bml:status
    only when deviating from the effective inherited status.

Abstract branch for structural constraints on definition elements (Blocks and
    members). Generic parameter T binds automatically to the effective definition type of the
    embedding context at validate time. Separates definition-shape rules from value-level rules
    (ValueConstraint).

Abstract branch for validation semantics. A Validation block describes whether and
    how BlockML itself should enforce an attached constraint. Constraints reference Validation via
    the optional validation property on org.blockml.bml.core.Constraint. When validation is omitted,
    the BlockML validator ignores the constraint — it remains metadata for renderers, editors,
    runtimes, and custom validators. Standard implementations live in org.blockml.bml.validation.*;
    domain libraries may define additional Validation blocks (for example
    com.machineblocks.bml.validation.ManufacturingWarning). The BlockML validator only interprets
    Validation types it understands; other tools may interpret additional Validation blocks.

Abstract branch for value-level constraints. Generic parameter T binds automatically
    to the effective ValueType of the enclosing Property at validate time — authors never specify T
    in BML. Valid only under a Property member's <constraints> container
    (BML_CONSTRAINT_TARGET_MISMATCH otherwise). Examples: Min, Max, Pattern, ValuePresent.

Abstract branch marker for alias Entity instances in an aliases aggregation on
    org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition only (root blocks and Sub-Blocks). Domain libraries
    define concrete alias blocks extending this branch for catalogue-controlled alternative names.
    The core library provides org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextAlias for ad-hoc text names and
    org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedAlias as the protected base for catalogue aliases whose members are
    set on derived alias block definitions; comma-separated shorthand on <aliases> expands to
    FreeTextAlias instances only. Not XML
    namespace prefix aliases. Not search tags — use org.blockml.bml.core.Keyword branch for those.

Abstract branch marker for keyword Entity instances in a keywords aggregation on
    org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition elements. Follows Everything-is-a-Block —
    domain libraries define concrete keyword blocks extending this branch for controlled vocabulary
    tags (for example org.example.keyword.Inheritance extending org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword).
    The core library provides org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextKeyword for ad-hoc text tags and
    org.blockml.bml.meta.FixedKeyword as the protected base for catalogue keywords whose members are
    set on derived keyword block definitions; comma-separated shorthand on <keywords> expands
    to FreeTextKeyword instances only — not to domain or FixedKeyword catalogue blocks.
    Distinct from org.blockml.bml.core.Alias (alternative Block type names on BlockDefinition).

Abstract empty branch for Bootstrap blocks — the optional single point of entry
    (SPOE) for automated startup: tasks, agents, CI pipelines, and similar process logic. Intentionally
    empty — no properties or aggregations. Concrete subtypes add scenario-specific members when
    needed.

    Distinct from org.blockml.bml.core.ReadMe, which is the required human/LLM reading entry on a
    Library (readMe aggregation). A Library may omit bootstrap (0..1) when it has no automated
    startup SPOE; it must never declare more than one Bootstrap.

    Human/LLM orientation (curated ReadFirst reading order, TaskIndex catalog) lives on ReadMe
    blocks — not on Bootstrap.

Abstract generic Entity for primitive values that must appear as Block instances
    inside a composition or aggregation. Follows the general generic resolution rule: T belongs
    exclusively to this Block and is never inherited. Derived Blocks bind or forward T explicitly
    through baseType (for example baseType = PrimitiveEntity(Integer) binds T = Integer and yields
    value : Integer). On instances that member is authored as value="…" (or <value>…</value>
    as the member itself) because the Property is named value — not because of the
    PropertyDefinition value field. Do not wrap other instance Properties in <value>; see
    doc:MemberAuthoring.

    Cannot be instantiated directly — concrete specializations (IntegerEntity, TextEntity,
    DecimalEntity, …) bind all generic parameters and become normal, instantiable Blocks.

    Properties continue to store primitive values directly — PrimitiveEntity exists only when the
    primitive value itself must become an Entity with identity, documentation, or metadata.

Abstract Group branch for block groups — named categories that organize Blocks
    for editors and tooling. Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks.
    Concrete group kinds extend this branch. BlockDefinition.groups overrides
    StructuralDefinition.groups to TypeReferenceEntity(group:BlockGroup)[].

Abstract Group branch for member groups — named categories that organize Block
    members (properties, aggregations, associations, capabilities) for editors and tooling.
    A member may reference several groups via MemberDefinition.groups (e.g. UI category and usage
    facet). Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks. Concrete group kinds
    extend this branch. MemberDefinition.groups overrides StructuralDefinition.groups to
    TypeReferenceEntity(group:MemberGroup)[].

Abstract identification marker for the Definition branch under org.blockml.bml.core.Block.
Intentionally empty — no properties, aggregations, or Sub-Blocks. Any block whose baseType
chain includes org.blockml.bml.core.Definition is a Definition meta-model block
(org.blockml.bml.definition.*). Concrete grammar lives on subtypes such as
org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition and org.blockml.bml.definition.BlockDefinition.

Used as a generic constraint and branch marker for definition-element references. Member path
ValueTypes (org.blockml.bml.type.MemberReference and children) constrain D to
org.blockml.bml.definition.MemberDefinition. Framework core branch types remain baseType markers;
domain interface-style type bounds use contracts and satisfiesTypeBound — see 17_type_system_bml.md.

Abstract meta-model base for all Block definition documents — root blocks,
    Sub-Blocks, and embedded virtual files. Semantically a Class: declarative type shape without instance
    state. Parsed into BomDocument.block and nested block definition trees. Generic type parameter B
    binds this definition to the Block type it describes — conceptually BlockDefinition of
    com.foo.Bar when B resolves to com.foo.Bar.

    Declares identity first (name, type, baseType, version), then semantic and discovery fields
    (is, isNot, aliases), generic parameters, contracts, and
    member declaration containers (properties, aggregations, associations, capabilities). Inherits
    summary and keywords aggregation (core.Keyword[]) from
    org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. isNot is block-level only; aliases aggregation
    (core.Alias[]) lists domain Alias blocks or org.blockml.bml.meta.FreeTextAlias instances. Omitted when unnecessary. Type modifiers abstract and final are inherited from
    org.blockml.bml.definition.StructuralDefinition. Every definition element is addressable via
    its canonical structural path within the Block FQN (for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width).
    Member declaration order in BML is preserved in BOM and is significant for StructType
    positional mapping and render targets.

    Declares definition (meta-model role selector) and subBlocks (recursive nested type hierarchy).
    Specialized as three sibling kinds that each override definition with a tighter TypeReference and
    default: SubBlockDefinition (nested), RootBlockDefinition (document root + embeddedBlocks),
    EmbeddedBlockDefinition (virtual .bml under root embeddedBlocks). Identity properties type and
    baseType are TypeReference strings (not TypeReferenceEntity aggregations) — type names the Block
    being declared; baseType carries the parent TypeExpression including generic applications. Other
    type references (composition tags, member type attributes, contracts) accept FQN, xmlns QName,
    context-bound unqualified fallback, or Sub-Block-relative names — all normalized to a canonical
    FQN during resolution (BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE, BML_AMBIGUOUS_TYPE, BML_UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE_PREFIX).

Abstract numeric primitive branch under org.blockml.bml.type.PrimitiveType.
    Concrete types: Integer (whole numbers), Decimal (default for non-integer numeric values),
    Float (binary floating-point — only when IEEE754 semantics are explicitly required).
    Abstract numeric branch — not resolvable via Property.type implicit namespace; use Integer, Decimal, or Float explicitly.
    Numeric types describe semantics only; values are stored in Properties.

    Generic parameter N constrains the measurement unit (extends org.blockml.bml.core.Unit).
    Default is org.blockml.bml.unit.None — bare Number / Integer / Decimal / Float are dimensionless.
    Supply N at reference sites when a unit is required, e.g. Integer(unit:Millimeter).

Abstract publishable library unit — groups exported Block and ValueType definitions,
optional XSD schemas, dependencies on other libraries, and nested sub-libraries.
Replaces the legacy library.xml descriptor.

Framework base type in org.blockml.bml.core — not exported via Library blocks.
Concrete Library.bml files inherit from BlockLibrary and declare aggregations explicitly.

Catalog aggregations are public and readOnly: foreign Blocks and tools may inspect a library
descriptor (e.g. list exports or dependencies) in expressions; only the Library definition
(and child overrides) may author the catalog. Instances must not rewrite these members.

Documentation prose language is Definition meta (def:BlockDefinition.language) on the Library
document — not a catalog aggregation. Exported blocks inherit that document language unless
they declare their own <language>.

Aggregations (each aggregation member is opened by name; none is default):
• readMe — required human/LLM reading entry (ReadMe block, 1..1)
• bootstrap — optional automation SPOE (Bootstrap block, 0..1)
• dependencies — other Library blocks this library depends on (typical: inner library
  depends on outer)
• subLibraries — nested child Library blocks grouped under this library
• schemas — optional legacy XSD paths as FilePathEntity instances
• blocks — exported Block and ValueType definitions (membership SSOT)

readMe and bootstrap hold TypeReferenceEntity children — empty QName sugar sets value to
that FQN. dependencies, subLibraries, and blocks use the same pattern. Optional bml:version on
sugar (or explicit TypeReferenceEntity) children is an exact-version assert against the
referenced type (value) — same semantics as external composition references; omitted → resolve
from TypeRegistry / library context; no match → BML_UNKNOWN_VERSION. schemas holds
FilePathEntity composition children; value is the relative .xsd path from the library package
root (directory containing Library.bml).

Concrete Library.bml <references> rule — at most two <see> entries:
1. Required: relation=ReadFirst targeting the same ReadMe named in readMe.
2. Optional: relation=ThenContinueWith targeting the Bootstrap named in bootstrap, only when
   bootstrap is present. Signals: after reading, continue by executing the automation SPOE.
No AuthoringGuide / DeepDive / Extends / SeeAlso (or other) entries on concrete Libraries —
those belong on documentation blocks, not on the catalog descriptor.

Abstract Relation subtype that may be used only on <see type="…"> entries —
    never on instance, file, url, property, aggregation, association, or capability targets.

    Generic T is the allowed target Block branch. The resolved type of see type= must satisfy
    satisfiesTypeBound(resolve(type), T) — otherwise BML_TYPE_BOUND_NOT_SATISFIED. Default
    T = core:Block — any Block type reference is allowed until a concrete subtype binds T more
    narrowly (e.g. ThenContinueWith binds T = core:Bootstrap).

    Plain Relation (SeeAlso, AuthoringGuide, …) remains unrestricted across target kinds.
    TypeRelation is for relations whose semantics require a Block type identity target.

Abstract universal root for all constraint types. Specialized by
    org.blockml.bml.constraint.ValueConstraint (property value rules) and
    org.blockml.bml.constraint.StructuralConstraint (definition-shape rules on Blocks and members).
    Every concrete constraint extends one of the branch types; the <constraints> embedding
    context determines the target and automatic generic binding — authors never specify target or
    type arguments in BML. Constraints describe the condition only. Whether BlockML enforces a
    constraint is controlled by the optional validation property, which references an
    org.blockml.bml.core.Validation block. When validation is omitted, validateConstraints() does not
    enforce the rule — the constraint remains metadata for renderers, editors, runtimes, and custom
    validators. The constraint instance itself is still validated (type, properties, generic
    binding, branch compatibility).

Abstract ValueType branch for closed enum ValueTypes — finite sets of named literal values.
Unqualified name EnumType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.EnumType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). EnumType is its own ValueType branch — not a StructType and not a
PrimitiveType:

• A PrimitiveType defines an open value domain (Text → all text values).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; the external property value is the
  member identity (id + EnumType), not a struct payload.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain.

Concrete EnumTypes declare allowed members as Block instances in the default values
aggregation — no special enum syntax. Examples: Direction, Face, StudType, BaseCutout,
Align.

Each catalog member is a Block instance of the EnumType with a mandatory bml:id (the
reference token). An EnumType may declare arbitrary properties on the type — filled per
member in values — analogous to private fields on a Java enum constant. Those properties
are catalog metadata on the type definition (for example a MachineBlocks value string for
SCAD). They are not part of the stored property value when an EnumType is used.

BOM storage for a property typed with an EnumType is only id + typeFqn (the EnumType).
Catalog properties are looked up from the EnumType definition when a renderer or tool needs
them. The editor renders EnumType properties as a SelectBox; the compiler validates authored
tokens against values by id.

Properties typed with an EnumType must not carry <suggestions> — valid values come
exclusively from values → BML_SUGGESTIONS_ON_ENUM. Properties may still carry
<constraints> where a compatible Constraint sub-type exists.

Enum value references in property values (defaultValue, composition attributes, expressions):
when the property type is an EnumType, qualified references may omit the {EnumTypeFQN}::
prefix — Standard is equivalent to com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout::Standard when the
expected type is known from the property declaration. The short form is invalid for untyped
strings. The validator resolves tokens against values by id; unknown values → validation
error.

Domain XSD enums remain accepted during migration with BML_LEGACY_TYPE_SOURCE warning — new
enums should be defined as BML EnumType blocks.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates closed value sets:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.BaseCutout")
• defaultValue and instance attribute values on EnumType properties
• Expression enum literals where the expected EnumType is known from context
• Library blocks export alongside other ValueType definitions

Abstract ValueType branch for composite value objects — complex values described by normal
Properties. Unqualified name StructType resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.StructType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). StructType is a dedicated branch — EnumType is a sibling under ValueType,
not a subtype of StructType.
StructTypes describe the structure of a value — their properties define the data layout.
StructTypes usually contain no values themselves; Property values remain stored in the owning
Property. Default values on StructType property definitions are allowed. Concrete StructTypes
declare <properties> whose members become struct fields — no special struct syntax.
Examples: Size3d, Color, Address, Transform. Parameterized value types (for example Box<T>)
are StructTypes that declare <genericTypes> — not a separate ValueType branch.

Struct property access is exclusively by name (size.x, size.y, size.z). Numeric index access
on StructType members (size[0]) is not valid — StructType is a typed object with named
properties only. Positional function-parameter syntax (#tool.capa("x", "y")) is handled by
FunctionMapping at call sites, not by general StructType semantics.

Field declaration order remains significant for:
• Positional array literals (size="[4, 2, 3]") — values map to properties by declaration order
• FunctionMapping positional parameter order for capability calls
• Compatibility — existing field order must not change across versions; new fields may be
  appended only at the end

Named object literals (size="{ x: 4, y: 2, z: 3 }") and attribute syntax on StructType
instances (<Size3d x="4" y="2" z="3"/>) are type-equivalent authoring forms.

Anonymous StructTypes — { field: Type, … } is a StructType without a declared name, written
directly in a type expression; it is the mechanism for structured Capability inputs. Each field
is Identifier ":" TypeExpression, so a field type is a full type expression and not merely an
unqualified type name: qualified references, multiplicity, generics, unions, instance
configuration, and nested anonymous StructTypes are all valid.
• { list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } — qualified reference with multiplicity
• { values: foo:Thing[1..n] } · { value: Integer | Text } · { nested: { x: Integer, y: Integer } }
The field-name separator and the prefix colon of a qualified reference sit at different grammar
levels (list : core:ValueType[]) — unambiguous, not a naming conflict. Field declaration order is
significant exactly as for named StructTypes. Rejecting a qualified field type while accepting an
unqualified one is a parser / mapper limitation, not a type-expression ambiguity.
See doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes.

Used wherever BlockML declares or validates structured values:
• Property <type> references (for example type="com.machineblocks.bml.type.Size3d")
• Block instances of the StructType as composition children or property payloads
• Capability inputType / outputType — named StructType or anonymous struct expressions
• Generic type applications (for example Box<Integer>) on StructTypes with
  <genericTypes>

Abstract ValueType branch for constant (singleton) value types. Unqualified name ConstantType
resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.ConstantType.

One of four language-level ValueType kinds (PrimitiveType · StructType · EnumType ·
ConstantType). ConstantType is neither a PrimitiveType, StructType, nor EnumType:

• A PrimitiveType defines a value domain (Text → all text values; Integer → all integers).
• A StructType defines the shape of the external value via its properties.
• An EnumType defines a closed set of named members; BOM stores id + typeFqn only.
• A ConstantType defines a singleton value domain — a value is valid if and only if it
  conforms to the underlying generic ValueType and equals the configured constant value.

The standard implementation is Constant<T extends ValueType> with a single Property
value : T. The generic type parameter is mandatory. Instance configuration supplies the
allowed value — for example Constant(Text){value: "auto"} or Constant(Integer){value: 5}.

The configured value Property belongs to the internal ValueType instance on the Property
definition — not to the property's external representation. The external value is always
identical to the representation of the underlying generic type T. For
Constant(Text){value: "auto"}, the external value is "auto" — not { value: "auto" }.

Validation proceeds in two steps:
1. Validate the supplied value against the generic ValueType T.
2. Compare the supplied value with the configured constant value.

Used primarily as a union alternative alongside ordinary ValueTypes:

Boolean | Constant(Text){value: "auto"}

Abstract ValueType for references to Block member definitions — properties,
    aggregations, associations, and capabilities. Extends TypeReference(B); adds D to constrain
    which MemberDefinition branch the path may target.

    Value forms:
    • Canonical definition path — for example com.foo.Bar.properties.width
    • Local member name when paired with a type qualifier (for example see type="com.foo.Bar"
      property="width" → com.foo.Bar.properties.width)

    Generic parameters:
    • B (from TypeReference) — owning Block branch for the member's enclosing type
    • D (baseType def:MemberDefinition) — member definition kind constraint

    Concrete specializations bind D:
    • PropertyReference     → D = def:PropertyDefinition
    • AggregationReference  → D = def:AggregationDefinition
    • AssociationReference  → D = def:AssociationDefinition
    • CapabilityReference   → D = def:CapabilityDefinition

    Primary use — StructuralDefinition Reference (see) member target attributes. Not for Block type
    identity (use TypeReference), instance pointers (use InstanceReference), or type-reference
    aggregations (use TypeReferenceEntity).

Action capability. Behaviour that neither consumes an external payload nor
    produces one — a pure side effect or command (trigger, reset, refresh, invalidate).
    Inherits _hasInput=false and _hasOutput=false; inputType and outputType are forbidden.

Aggregation-level structural constraint. T binds to the effective
    AggregationDefinition. When validation is set, each composition child under the aggregation must
    resolve to the given Block type FQN. Reference implementation for AggregationConstraint branch.

Angular unit — degree of arc (°). Use for rotation and orientation angles,
    e.g. Decimal(unit:Degree) or Float(unit:Degree).

Annotations formalize directive namespaces. They are orthogonal to the Definition meta-model
(org.blockml.bml.definition.*) — they do not describe block structure, members, or constraints.
Naming overlap (Property, Aggregation, …) classifies directive form only;
