The BML Expression Language is extended JSON inside ${ } delimiters. It appears wherever a
Block member value needs to be dynamic — derived, computed, or bound to a service. Capability
<implementation> bodies use the same language inside <$ $> embeds
(doc:EmbeddedExpressions).

Four additions beyond JSON:
• Property references — myProp, myProp.x (StructType members by name only; no size[0] on structs)
• Model bindings — @model:/path, @model:relativeAttr
• Bean calls — @bean.capa(...) (call) · @bean.capa (capability linking, no parentheses)
• Built-in calls — #math.min(a, b), #strings.trim(s)

Everything else follows a JSON subset: double-quoted strings, numbers, booleans (true/True/TRUE
accepted; BOM stores lowercase), arrays [...], objects {...}. null is not a BML literal —
absent/empty is not typed as null.

Expression vs BOM data layer (separate):
• BOM stores LiteralValue and ExpressionValue.raw — immutable authored form
• parseExpression() → AST + type inference — utility output, not BOM mutation
• evaluateExpression() — renderer working model only (Stage 3)
Validator checks correctness (members, visibility, types, capabilities) but never executes.

Scope rules:
• Bare property access — current Block instance only (no parent/sibling climb); top-down
• @bean — walk composition hierarchy; bml:scope=context visible to descendants; local = declaring
  Block only
• #built-ins — always available; cannot be overridden
• @model: relative paths need binding context from nearest parent Model-bound Aggregation
• bml:each / bml:with variables — element + descendants; shadow outer same names
  (doc:BmlDirectives)
• <value> expressions — own Properties and #built-ins; topological resolve; cycles →
  BML_PROPERTY_CYCLE

FunctionMapping maps call arguments to Capability inputType (doc:FunctionMappingModel). Named
and positional must not be mixed under default mapping.

V1 supported: literals; operators + - * / % == != < > <= >= && || ! ?:;
property access myProp / myProp.x / myProp[i] (index only where valid — not StructType fields);
#math.min/max/abs/floor/ceil/round/pow/sqrt/clamp; #numbers.formatDecimal; #strings.concat/length;
#lists.size/get/first/last/sequence; bml:each/if/unless/container/with.
V1 deferred: @bean execution, model bindings, capability linking, most #strings/#bools,
TypeScript service transpilation.

Diagnostics (selection): BML_EXPR_SYNTAX_ERROR, BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY,
BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_BEAN, BML_EXPR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN, BML_EXPR_TYPE_MISMATCH,
BML_EXPR_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH, BML_EXPR_LINK_*, BML_EXPR_MODEL_NO_CONTEXT,
BML_EXPR_BUILTIN_NOT_V1, BML_EXPR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO — plus FunctionMapping codes.
Formal EBNF / AST shapes remain DeepDive in 10_expression_language.md (parser utility contract).

The closest familiar model: a Block is a declarative semantic Class; a Block Instance is an
Object. This is a semantic analogy — not a mandate for runtime OOP. The compiler may represent
definitions and instances as plain data; the parser nonetheless distinguishes block documents
(classes) from composition children (objects).

Block (definition):
• .bml file · BlockDefinition
• FQN · members · composition schema
• Describes shape and behaviour
• No runtime · no address

Block Instance (in composition):
• Element such as ac:Wall with bml:id and member values
• typeFqn + bml:id + member values
• One concrete occurrence
• May become a Thing in Runtime (WOT vocabulary)

Composition:
• Aggregations hold Block Instances as children
• Instance identity uses bml:id (not the type FQN)
• Nested paths compose with :: (wall::bottom::inner)
• bml:version pins external references to exact library versions

Instance serialization (authoring) — definition fields are not instance wrappers:
• On Block definitions — Property default uses the value field (<value> preferred);
  Aggregation default uses <composition> nested inside the aggregation member
• On Block instances — NEVER wrap a Property in <value> and NEVER wrap Aggregation
  children in <composition>. The Property is a Block attribute or the Property element's
  direct content (myProperty="…" or <myProperty>…</myProperty>). Aggregation children
  sit directly inside the aggregation element (or bml:container for shared directives)
• Exception: a member whose name is value (PrimitiveEntity, TypeReferenceEntity, …) uses
  value="…" as ordinary instance syntax for that member — not as a PropertyDefinition wrapper
• readOnly effective members must not be authored on instances → BML_READONLY_MEMBER_WRITE
• Empty child meaning depends on aggregation type (instance vs TypeReferenceEntity sugar) —
  doc:MemberAuthoring / doc:CompositionModel / doc:SubBlockModel

Context-dependent interpretation:
• ValueTypes as type-classes for Property values and Capability input/output
• Languages as meta-classes for implementation contracts
• Sub-Blocks in the same .bml file as nested classes (derived types, inner scope)
• Presets as named default bindings on a class

Relationships: Library contains Blocks; Block has Members, Presets, Compositions; Catalog
contains top-level composite Blocks.

The Render Target is free in what it produces and how it maps BML to output. No global rule
requires output to be blocks in the target language, 1:1 mapping input Block → one output
artifact, or any files at all (side-effects-only targets are valid).

Cardinality, format, and semantics are target-defined. The framework provides utilities;
each renderer decides which to use and in what sequence:

SCAD Renderer: resolveInheritance → evaluateExpression → expandComposition → renderSCAD
Java Renderer: resolveInheritance → resolveContracts → renderJava
Documentation Renderer: renderRawBOM() → Markdown / HTML

Each renderer owns an internal working model — optimised, cacheable, freely mutable:
SCAD: Modules, Parameters, GeometryGraph
Java: Classes, Fields, Methods
React: Components, Props, JSX Tree

The working model belongs exclusively to the renderer. The Canonical BOM remains unchanged.

MachineBlocks SCAD re-creates Blocks in the target language via mb_block() — a common pattern,
not a platform obligation. ScreenMachine may emit React JSX; EBOM may emit KiCad symbols.
The renderer reads BML Blocks; it does not need to preserve Block as a runtime concept in
its internal pipeline — only to emit correct target output.

Platonic mapping: BML holds the Idea (Urbild) stable. The compiler is Manifestor tooling —
it may represent the Idea internally as it chooses. Full Manifestation is the renderer's and
runtime's job in a specific World.

The validator expands the authored type reference to a canonical FQN and looks up the
BlockDefinition in TypeRegistry. Failure means the type is not registered at validation time.
Common causes: typo in FQN or xmlns prefix, missing Library blocks entry, unloaded dependency
library, or reference to a Sub-Block type without the full parent-qualified path where required.
Emitted when type, baseType, contract, language, or member type references an unknown or
    misspelled FQN — or when bootstrap order has not yet loaded the library that defines the type.

The Web of Things (WOT) provides the philosophical foundation for BlockML. Optional reading
for context — not required to use the compiler or author BML.

Idea (Plato):
The only true constant. Exists independently of Universes, Worlds, Technologies, and
Manifestations. An Idea does not change. In BlockML: Block, ValueType, Language, FQN —
describable without any render target. BML holds the Idea stable. The Block definition
itself is the Idea; the authoring field <is> (BOM block.is, reflection bml:Self.is)
names that Idea in an ultra-short noun phrase for humans and LLMs — it is not the Idea.

Manifestation:
The entire process from Idea to Thing — not a single step. Manifestor (compiler) produces
preconditions; Runtime completes Manifestation in a World the Manifestor cannot fully know.
In BlockML: renderer working model, target output, runtime behaviour. The renderer decides
interpretation — SCAD mb_block(), React components, KiCad symbols are different Manifestations
of the same Ideas.

Grammar (BlockML / BOM):
How Things are structured. Blocks are the grammar of a World. Types, Languages, Services,
and Capabilities are part of that grammar — not implementation detail. stud:// is how Things
communicate; BOM Core is how Things are structured.

World:
Delivers interpretation. An Idea carries no properties of its own — no substance, material,
or weight. The World assigns meaning. MachineBlocks is one World (physical geometry → SCAD);
other Worlds (ScreenMachine → React, EBOM → electronics) share type FQNs with different
render mappings.

WOT alignment at language layer: ontological unity in BML; engineering freedom in compiler
internals and renderer output. Without adoption, there is no WOT — and without internal
freedom, there is no maintainable compiler.

Two uses:
    1. Concrete Library.bml — required single ReadFirst <see> targeting the ReadMe named in
       the readMe aggregation (catalog entry point). May be followed by ThenContinueWith → Bootstrap
       when bootstrap is present; no other <see> relations on concrete Libraries.
    2. README / ReadMe blocks — curated mental learning order. ReadFirst entries should appear
       first in <references>, in reading order.

    Distinct from Library.readMe (aggregation that names the ReadMe block) and from ReadNext
    (forward edge between documentation blocks outside the README catalog).

TypeRelation(core:Bootstrap) — use on concrete Library <see type="…"> entries
    to point at the library's Bootstrap SPOE after the human/LLM reading entry. Target must be a
    type reference whose resolved type satisfies satisfiesTypeBound(…, core:Bootstrap); file/url/
    instance/member targets are forbidden (TypeRelation rule).

    Sequence on Library.bml: ReadFirst → ReadMe (required), then ThenContinueWith → Bootstrap when
    the library declares a bootstrap aggregation. Distinct from ReadNext (narrative learning chain)
    and from TaskIndex / TaskStep (task catalog). Signals: after reading, continue with the
    automation entry.

Typical file= targets — repository markdown with authoring rules, examples, or
    migration notes. Use when the link is procedural ("how to write…") rather than structural
    (Extends) or optional background (SeeAlso).

Typical pattern: inner lists outer in dependencies; outer lists inner in subLibraries. Membership is defined by Library.blocks.
Emitted when outer library blocks reference a Block exported only by an inner nested library incorrectly.

Unqualified block references are supported only at specialized, semantically unambiguous
reference sites. Each site defines exactly one implicit namespace. The name expands directly:

<Name> → <implicitNamespace>.<Name>

There is no multi-stage search, no global TypeRegistry fallback, and no document-scope
heuristics. If the expanded FQN does not exist or the Block does not satisfy the expected
base type for that site, the compiler emits an error.

Reference sites and implicit namespaces:
• Property type → org.blockml.bml.type.*
• Capability inputType / outputType → org.blockml.bml.type.*
• Implementation language attribute → org.blockml.bml.language.*
• language element child → org.blockml.bml.language.* (NaturalLanguage)
• language attribute on documentation → org.blockml.bml.language.*
  (Markdown(NaturalLanguage) | NaturalLanguage — the generic argument resolves in the same
  namespace)
• language attribute on change → org.blockml.bml.language.* (NaturalLanguage)
• language attribute on see → org.blockml.bml.language.* (NaturalLanguage)
• relation attribute on see → org.blockml.bml.relation.* (Relation)
• language attribute on example → org.blockml.bml.language.* (Language)
• status element content · bml:status attribute → org.blockml.bml.status.*
• Capability type → org.blockml.bml.capability.*
• Constraint validation attribute → org.blockml.bml.validation.*

Examples:
• <width type="Integer" /> → org.blockml.bml.type.Integer
• <implementation language="TypeScript"> → org.blockml.bml.language.TypeScript
• <language><English /></language> → org.blockml.bml.language.English
• <documentation language="Markdown(German)"> → org.blockml.bml.language.Markdown with
  L = org.blockml.bml.language.German (shorthand <documentation language="German"> resolves
  to the same entry)
• <change version="2.0.0" language="German"> → org.blockml.bml.language.German
• <see file="guide.md" language="English"> → org.blockml.bml.language.English
• <see type="core:Block" relation="Extends"> → org.blockml.bml.relation.Extends
• <example language="OpenSCAD"> → org.blockml.bml.language.OpenSCAD
• <status>Draft</status> → org.blockml.bml.status.Draft
• type="Transformation" on Capability → org.blockml.bml.capability.Transformation
• validation="Error" on constraint → org.blockml.bml.validation.Error

Resolution applies per type reference, including inside composed type expressions. In an
anonymous StructType on inputType / outputType, every field type is resolved on its own —
{ list: core:ValueType[], index: Integer } resolves list via the xmlns prefix core and index via
the site's implicit namespace to org.blockml.bml.type.Integer. A qualified field type is never
ambiguous with the field-name separator (doc:TypeExpressions — Anonymous StructTypes).

General block references have no implicit namespace — baseType, aggregation type,
InstanceReference type arguments, and composition instance tags require a full FQN or xmlns prefix.
Explicit FQNs and xmlns prefixes remain valid everywhere, including at specialized sites.

Use for file= or url= targets with long-form prose the reader may skip on first
    pass. Distinct from Requires (mandatory) and AuthoringGuide (procedural). Typical for architecture
    documents, WOT foundation, or specification deep-dives.

Use for hard dependencies — types, documentation, or external resources the reader
    or runtime must know first. Distinct from ReadFirst (curated path) and SeeAlso (optional peer link).

Use on <see> entries at the start of a TaskGuide <references> container
    — before TaskStep entries. Distinct from Requires (dependency of the current definition) and
    ReadFirst (library-wide learning path). Prerequisite scopes to one task procedure.

Use on <see> entries in documentation blocks (org.blockml.bml.documentation.*)
    to point to the next topic in a learning chain — typically body text starting with
    "Next reading step". Distinct from ReadFirst (README curated entry points), Prerequisite
    (task-scoped do-this-first), and SeeAlso (optional peer link). ReadNext is a single forward
    edge between narrative documentation blocks, not a library-wide ordered catalog.

Use on <see> entries in org.blockml.bml.diagnostic.* blocks to link a
    validator code to a procedural fix guide. Target should reference an org.blockml.bml.task.*
    TaskGuide block. Enables error-driven navigation: reported BML_* code → Diagnostic block →
    Resolves → TaskGuide with TaskStep entries.

Use on <see> entries in README / ReadMe blocks to list accomplishable tasks.
    Distinct from ReadFirst (mental learning order) and SeeAlso (optional peer link). Tooling
    filters relation=TaskIndex to build a task menu for humans, agents, or CI. Target should
    reference an org.blockml.bml.task.* TaskGuide block.

Use on <see> entries inside org.blockml.bml.task.* TaskGuide blocks.
    Document order in <references> is step order — same convention as ReadFirst on README.
    Target may be a Block, repository markdown file, or external URL. Distinct from Prerequisite
    (before starting the task) and Requires (hard dependency on the current definition).

Use to disambiguate easily confused concepts — for example Sub-Block vs embedded Block,
    contract vs baseType, Inbound vs Outbound capability. The context text body must explain the
    difference explicitly.

Use when the referenced Block is in the baseType chain or represents a branch the
    current type belongs to. Typical type= targets only — not for file or url references.

Use when the referenced Block or Definition element is the formal specification
    the current type conforms to — for example def:PropertyDefinition on a property member, or
    core:Bootstrap on a README block.

ValueType branch of BlockML. Semantic unit for property and Capability types
    (primitives, structs, enums). A ValueType never stores data — it describes the nature of a
    value. All concrete values are stored exclusively in Properties. Only ValueTypes may appear as
    property type or Capability inputType/outputType.

    Top of the value assignability hierarchy — every PrimitiveType, StructType, EnumType, and
    ConstantType is assignable to ValueType. With multiplicity, compatibility is evaluated against
    the referenced element type: ValueType[] accepts zero or more values whose concrete ValueType is
    assignable to ValueType, each element validated independently, so element types may differ
    within one collection. See doc:TypeExpressions — Collection compatibility ·
    Heterogeneous collections.

ValueType for non-owning pointers to concrete Block instances identified by bml:id.
Unqualified name InstanceReference resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.InstanceReference.

Lexical forms:
• Local id — myId (visibility-scoped within the enclosing composition)
• Qualified — {EnclosingBlockFQN}::{instanceId} (e.g. com.foo.Bar::myId)
• Prefixed qualified — foo:Bar::myId (xmlns QName of the enclosing Block document, then :: and id)

Not a Block type FQN (use TypeReference), not a member definition path (use MemberReference /
AssociationReference), and not a resource URI (use URI).

Generic parameter:
• T (baseType core:Block) — target instance must satisfy T

In type="..." attributes, write generic applications with round parentheses:
• InstanceReference(core:Block) → 0..1 pointer to a core:Block instance
• InstanceReference(bml:Self)[] → 0..n pointers to instances of the effective Block type

Primary use — AssociationDefinition type (associations may only declare InstanceReference(T)
or InstanceReference(T)[] — instance-to-instance model links). Also the type of see instance=
on StructuralDefinition.Reference (documentation type→instance links — not Associations).

Resolution and visibility rules: docs/01_bom_core.md — Qualified Block Instance References
(public aggregation, static authored bml:id, BML_UNRESOLVABLE_INSTANCE_REF, …).

ValueType for type references — fully qualified names (FQNs) and TypeExpressions that name a
Block. Unqualified name TypeReference resolves to org.blockml.bml.type.TypeReference. Formerly
FullyQualifiedName; the FQN string format is unchanged.

FQN format (Java-style reverse-domain, dot-separated):
• Package segments — lowercase, reverse-domain (for example org.blockml.bml.core,
  com.machineblocks.bml.type)
• Class segment — PascalCase (for example Block, Integer, Wall)
• Full form — <package>.<ClassName> (for example org.blockml.bml.type.Integer,
  com.machineblocks.bml.core.Block)
Sub-Block FQNs derive as parentFqn + "." + name when omitted in source.

Namespace prefixes in BML (core:, type:, def:, …) map to package segments; the Namespace
Resolver stores the resolved FQN string in BOM typeFqn fields. Unknown FQN at validate time
→ BML_UNKNOWN_TYPE.

Generic parameter:
• B (baseType core:Block) — Block branch constraint for the referenced type

In type="..." attributes, write generic applications with round parentheses — not angle
brackets (XML-safe, readable):
• TypeReference(core:Block) → B = core.Block
• TypeReference(core:Language) → B = core.Language

Concrete type arguments must satisfy B's baseType constraint → BML_GENERIC_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.

Primary use — Block-definition identity (`type`, `baseType`) and definition metadata where a
type attribute or property holds a Block FQN / TypeExpression string. When a type reference must
appear as an Entity in composition or aggregation, use org.blockml.bml.type.TypeReferenceEntity.

Instance pointers (bml:id / FQN::id) use org.blockml.bml.type.InstanceReference — not
TypeReference. Member definition paths (property, aggregation, association, capability) use the
org.blockml.bml.type.MemberReference branch — not TypeReference.

When a constraint with validation="Error" is violated, the BlockML
    validator emits BML_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION and compilation fails.

When a constraint with validation="Information" is violated, the BlockML
    validator emits BML_CONSTRAINT_INFORMATION. Compilation continues.

When a constraint with validation="Warning" is violated, the BlockML
    validator emits BML_CONSTRAINT_WARNING. Compilation continues.
